title: FateIntel specialist substance-group requirements
scope: PFAS members, salts, isomers, precursors, terminal products, side-chain fluorinated polymers and fluoropolymers

implementation_boundary.statement: This registry records reviewed software requirements and source provenance. It must not be presented as an implemented regulatory method, completed assessment, legal classification or authority acceptance.
implementation_boundary.required_runtime_behaviour: Fail closed into specialist review whenever a nanoform/nanomaterial or PFAS trigger is present until the applicable jurisdictional method and evidence basis are implemented, versioned and validated.

status_vocabulary.specified_not_implemented: Requirement is evidenced and designed but has no executable calculation.
status_vocabulary.external_review_required: A specialist or external model must produce a reviewed, hashed result before orchestration can continue.
status_vocabulary.jurisdiction_check_required: The legal or guidance status must be checked against the current competent-authority source.
status_vocabulary.research_only: The method may support exploration but cannot claim regulatory alignment.

requirements: Retain the jurisdiction's legal definition separately from the scientific particle description.
Record whether the introduced or registered material is a nanoform, a justified set of similar nanoforms, a nanoscale form of an existing substance, or outside the applicable legal definition.
Do not infer nano status from a trade name, a single mean size, or a bulk-substance record.

identity_and_characterisation_fields.notes: Include impurities, dopants, additives and stabilisers.
Store method, lower/upper range and fraction by number; do not substitute mass distribution.
Include fibres, plates and irregular morphologies where relevant.
Record technique and mass- or volume-specific basis.
Bind to medium composition, pH and ionic strength.
Record stock preparation, sonication energy and dispersant.
Bind every study to the tested batch and characterisation snapshot.
Keep apparent solubility and time-resolved dissolution distinct.

environmental_fate_processes.assessment: Use medium-specific time courses under relevant pH, ionic strength and natural organic matter conditions. Preserve preparation and sonication details.

environmental_fate_processes.process: dissolution and release of dissolved species
environmental_fate_processes.assessment: Measure apparent solubility and dissolution kinetics over relevant pH and time; track the particulate and dissolved fractions separately.
preferred_methods: OECD GD on dissolution and dispersion stability

environmental_fate_processes.assessment: Represent interactions with natural colloids, suspended solids, porous media and biota; simple equilibrium partitioning is insufficient unless justified.
preferred_methods: weight-of-evidence and validated external transport modelling

environmental_fate_processes.assessment: Track redox reactions, sulfidation, oxidation, phototransformation, coating loss and biomolecule-corona changes as new material states linked to the original nanoform.
Account for aggregation and solids association, transformation, dissolved release, effluent passage and sludge transfer without equating removal from water with destruction.
preferred_methods: measured mass balance or validated nano-enabled external model

environmental_fate_processes.assessment: Treat sediment as a dynamic compartment; retain deposition, burial, resuspension and transformed-particle state.
preferred_methods: OECD GD 420 and site/scenario-specific mass balance

environmental_fate_processes.assessment: Do not use log Kow as the controlling descriptor for particulate materials. Select waterborne or dietary evidence from dispersion stability, dissolution and likely exposure route.
preferred_methods: OECD TG 305 interpreted through OECD GD 406

ecotoxicology_requirements: Characterise the tested material and verify exposure concentrations and material state through the test.
Separate particle-mediated effects from effects of dissolved ions or molecules where scientifically possible.
Consider settling, agglomeration, feeding inhibition, physical fouling, shading and analytical interference when interpreting effects.
Use measured or justified time-weighted concentrations when nominal exposure is unstable.
Record medium chemistry, dispersion preparation and test-vessel conditions needed to reproduce exposure.
Apply aquatic and sediment guideline adaptations rather than assuming an unmodified conventional test is valid.
Use endpoint-specific grouping/read-across; similarity for one endpoint does not establish similarity for all endpoints.
compatibility_rules: PEC and effect benchmark must refer to the same nanoform or justified set, transformation state and composition.
Total, particulate and dissolved concentrations are not interchangeable.
Mass, number and surface-area concentration bases may not be converted without measured particle distributions and an explicit model.
Media pH, ionic strength, dissolved organic matter and exposure preparation must be compared before chaining fate and effect evidence.
A bulk-substance PNEC cannot be silently applied to a nanoform.
A model that assumes equilibrium Koc partitioning cannot automatically consume a colloidal-particle output.

jurisdiction_routes.route: REACH nanoform-specific information requirements and ECHA endpoint/read-across guidance
key_requirements: Report nanoforms individually or in a scientifically justified set.
Bind information requirements and chemical safety assessment to the covered nanoform or set.
Document the characterisation parameters required by the amended REACH annexes.
Justify endpoint-specific grouping/read-across.

jurisdiction_routes.route: UK REACH with HSE recommendations and current nanoform guidance
key_requirements: Use the current UK legal text and HSE recommendations.
Provide robust study summaries with test-item and batch characterisation.
Use measured rather than nominal aquatic concentrations where instability makes nominal values unreliable.

jurisdiction_routes.route: TSCA new-chemical review, section 8(a) nanoscale reporting and case-specific controls
key_requirements: Determine whether a discrete nanoscale form is reportable under 40 CFR part 704.
Preserve manufacture, processing, use, exposure, release and health/safety information.
For a new chemical, route through PMN review; retain consent-order or SNUR conditions where imposed.
Do not infer a finding of harm or safety from nanoscale reporting status alone.

jurisdiction_routes.route: CEPA framework for existing and new manufactured nanomaterials
key_requirements: Adapt conventional exposure and hazard assessment to particle-specific identity, fate and dosimetry.
Use multiple quantity metrics when necessary and match PEC/PNEC bases.
Evaluate aggregation, dissolution, transformation and media effects explicitly.
Apply the current AICIS nanoscale definition and exclusions.
Treat applicable nanoscale introductions as the specified class/risk category required by current guidance.
Do not transfer EU or US nano status without rechecking the Australian criteria.

jurisdiction_routes.route: OECD test guidelines, guidance documents, grouping and Mutual Acceptance of Data
key_requirements: Record the exact guideline version, deviations, GLP and test-material characterisation.
Use nano-specific adaptations and guidance for dispersion, dissolution, aquatic/sediment testing and bioaccumulation.
Confirm receiving-authority acceptance; an OECD document is not itself a marketing authorisation.

pfas.display_name: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances and associated chemicals

requirements: Record the PFAS definition used by each jurisdiction or programme; do not treat the OECD structural terminology as a universally adopted legal scope.
Record structure-level evidence and group membership with confidence, exclusions and source version.
Distinguish individual analytes from class-, sum- and total-fluorine measurements.

assessment_entities: ultrashort-chain or highly mobile product including TFA when structurally relevant
extractable or total organic fluorine fraction

identity_and_measurement_fields.notes: Store OECD terminology separately from each legal/programme definition.
Include CAS, InChIKey, formula, charge, salt/counterion and isomer information where known.
Record functional group, perfluoroalkyl chain and precursor/terminal role.
Record method version, analytes, matrices, reporting limits, recovery, blanks and isotope dilution.
Target analyte, sum, TOP assay, EOF/TOF or non-target result; these are not interchangeable.
Store transformations as a directed network, not a single parent-only half-life.
Dissolved, colloidal, particulate, air-water interface, NAPL-water interface and solid-associated states.
pH, ionic strength/salinity, organic carbon, mineralogy, redox and relevant cosolutes.
For biota, record tissue, wet/dry/lipid basis and whole-body versus organ data.

environmental_fate_processes.assessment: Quantify manufacture, formulation, product use, aqueous film-forming foam use, wastewater, biosolids, landfill leachate, recycling, incineration and other relevant releases. Transfer is not destruction.

environmental_fate_processes.process: aqueous advection, dispersion and groundwater transport
environmental_fate_processes.assessment: Use a conceptual site model and site-specific hydrogeology. Track mobile ionic species and interactions with solids and interfaces; do not assume a single generic Koc describes transport.
Evaluate hydrophobic and electrostatic interactions, organic carbon/mineral surfaces, air-water and NAPL-water interfaces, concentration dependence, chain length and functional group.
Represent precursor-to-intermediate-to-terminal product networks. Absence of target PFAAs at one time does not establish absence of future persistent products.
Treat neutral volatile precursors separately from ionic terminal acids and salts; include atmospheric transformation/deposition where relevant.

environmental_fate_processes.process: wastewater, biosolids, landfill, recycling and destruction
environmental_fate_processes.assessment: Maintain mass flow across effluent, sludge/biosolids, leachate, air emissions and residues. A removal efficiency cannot be labelled degradation without analytical mass-balance evidence.
Use measured tissue- and species-relevant evidence. Protein binding, dietary exposure and air-breathing-organism biomagnification mean lipid-normalised BCF and log Kow alone are inadequate.

ecotoxicology_requirements: Preserve exact analyte, salt/isomer form, purity and precursor/terminal-product status.
Match water-column criteria, sediment/soil benchmarks and tissue values to the correct matrix and concentration basis.
Represent acute, chronic and tissue criteria with their distinct averaging periods and frequency assumptions.
Support individual-substance, sum, mixture and class-based lines of evidence without treating them as mathematically interchangeable.
Record dietary and tissue exposure where water-only assessment is not protective or not scientifically representative.
Do not use a single generic PFAS PNEC or extrapolate one member's endpoint to the entire class without an explicit, reviewed grouping rationale.
Maintain targeted, precursor-oxidation, total-organic-fluorine and non-target measurements as separate evidence types.

pmt_vpvm_screen.legal_scope: EU CLP hazard classification criteria; elsewhere a prioritisation or policy concept only where adopted

criteria.P: degradation half-life >60 d in marine water, >40 d in fresh/estuarine water, >180 d in marine sediment, >120 d in fresh/estuarine sediment, or >120 d in soil
criteria.M: log Koc <3; for ionisable substances, the lowest log Koc across pH 4-9
criteria.T: long-term aquatic NOEC or ECx <0.01 mg/L, or specified CMR/STOT RE/endocrine-disruption classifications
criteria.vP: degradation half-life >60 d in marine/fresh/estuarine water or >180 d in marine/freshwater/estuarine sediment or soil
criteria.vM: log Koc <2; for ionisable substances, the lowest log Koc across pH 4-9

guardrails: Implement only against the exact current legal text and full weight-of-evidence provisions.
Do not label PFAS as PMT/vPvM merely because it is a PFAS.
Do not describe PMT/vPvM as a REACH-created class; the harmonised criteria were introduced into EU CLP by Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/707.
For GB, label the current HSE/Defra PMT approach as interim unless and until it is formally adopted in law.

compatibility_rules: The PEC and benchmark must identify the same PFAS member or explicitly defined sum/group.
Targeted concentration, TOP assay response, EOF/TOF and non-target signal are not interchangeable quantities.
Linear/branched isomer and acid/salt conversions require a documented molar basis.
Water, porewater, sediment, soil, whole-body and tissue-specific values cannot be chained without an explicit transfer model.
Dissolved, colloidal, particulate and interfacial mass must remain distinguishable.
A precursor concentration cannot be compared directly with a terminal-product PNEC unless a reviewed transformation and stoichiometric model is applied.
A conventional organic-chemical Koc model cannot automatically drive PFAS groundwater transport.
Water-column and tissue criteria retain their distinct temporal/frequency and concentration bases.

jurisdiction_routes.route: Substance-specific REACH/CLP and environmental-media requirements, plus the evolving broad PFAS restriction process
jurisdiction_routes.assessment_character: Hazard classification, risk assessment and restriction are distinct workflows
key_requirements: Apply the current CLP PMT/vPvM criteria only through a complete weight-of-evidence evaluation.
Check the current ECHA/Commission restriction status; the 2023 universal PFAS restriction dossier is a proposal until the legal process is complete.
Retain substance-specific water, biota and other legal standards separately from proposed class restrictions.

jurisdiction_routes.route: UK REACH/GB CLP and interim PMT approach for PFAS risk management
jurisdiction_routes.assessment_character: Existing law plus interim policy prioritisation
key_requirements: State clearly that the published PMT approach is interim and not itself a harmonised GB legal classification.
Use it to prioritise evidence and risk-management questions, not to fabricate a binding classification.
Check current HSE/Defra decisions before relying on the route.

jurisdiction_routes.route: Programme-specific TSCA, CERCLA/RCRA/CWA/SDWA/FIFRA or site-assessment pathway
jurisdiction_routes.assessment_character: Fragmented by statute, PFAS member, medium and decision context
key_requirements: Route new PFAS through the current TSCA new-chemicals framework and retain case-specific exposure/release conclusions.
Use current, method-specific analytical evidence such as EPA Method 1633 where applicable.
Represent EPA aquatic-life water-column and tissue criteria with their exact status and basis.
Treat EPA destruction/disposal guidance as nonbinding guidance and retain technology-specific uncertainty.

jurisdiction_routes.route: CEPA class assessment and subsequent risk-management instruments
jurisdiction_routes.assessment_character: Class-level weight of evidence with exclusions and instrument-specific follow-on
key_requirements: Use the exact class scope and exclusions in the current Government of Canada report.
Preserve evidence on precursors, terminal PFAAs, transport, exposure and effects across environmental and human-health lines.
Do not turn a qualitative class conclusion into a member-specific numeric RQ without suitable member-specific evidence.

jurisdiction_routes.route: PFAS NEMP 3.1 contaminated-site/environmental management plus AICIS introduction assessment
jurisdiction_routes.assessment_character: National guidance plus industrial-chemical introduction gate
key_requirements: Build and iteratively refine a conceptual site model covering sources, pathways, receptors and temporal variability.
Use targeted and broader analytical lines of evidence where appropriate; preserve TOP/EOF/TOF limitations.
Assess soil, groundwater, surface water, sediment, biota, biosolids, landfill and reuse pathways as applicable.
Apply the current AICIS designated-fluorinated-chemical categorisation separately from contaminated-site assessment.

jurisdiction_routes.route: POPs listing and national implementation for listed PFAS
jurisdiction_routes.assessment_character: International elimination/restriction obligations implemented through national law
key_requirements: Check chemical, salt/isomer/related-compound scope, annex, exemptions and national implementation.
Keep Stockholm listing separate from broader OECD PFAS identity and domestic class assessments.

cross_group_orchestration_requirements: A specialist-group trigger must block ordinary neutral-organic defaults until reviewed applicability is recorded.
Every entity transition must preserve mass and identity provenance: nanoform to transformed particle/dissolved species, or PFAS precursor to terminal product.

A result may be displayed as exploratory, but it may not control a regulatory tier until method, jurisdiction, identity, concentration basis, medium, time basis and evidence provenance are compatible.
Research models must use controlled handoff/import with executable/version, input snapshot, raw-output hashes, endpoint mapping and independent review.
A classification/restriction/emission-minimisation conclusion is not reducible to an RQ and needs a separate decision object.

implementation_phases.name: Identity and applicability gates
implementation_phases.exit_criteria: No specialist material can silently enter the conventional-organic workflow.

implementation_phases.name: Evidence and analytical basis
implementation_phases.exit_criteria: Every fate/effect value identifies the tested/measured entity, method and concentration basis.

implementation_phases.name: Fate state and mass ledgers
implementation_phases.exit_criteria: Transfer, transformation and destruction are distinguishable and mass closure is auditable.

implementation_phases.name: Ecotoxicology and risk characterisation
implementation_phases.exit_criteria: Only compatible evidence can generate a decision-eligible risk result.

implementation_phases.name: Jurisdictional workflows and external models
implementation_phases.exit_criteria: Regulatory-aligned and research-only pathways are automatically and correctly distinguished.

minimum_acceptance_tests: A bulk TiO2 record cannot satisfy a nanoform identity requirement without a reviewed relationship.
A dissolved-ion ecotoxicity endpoint cannot be compared directly with total-particle PEC.
A mass concentration cannot be converted to particle-number concentration without measured particle data and an explicit model.
An OECD PFAS structural match does not automatically create a legal PFAS-scope decision for every jurisdiction.
A PFAS TOP assay result cannot be entered as a target-analyte concentration.
A precursor PEC cannot be divided by a terminal-product PNEC without an accepted transformation model.
A conventional Koc-only groundwater result cannot be marked regulatory-aligned for PFAS or a colloidal nanomaterial.
A PMT/vPvM screen cannot conclude without complete persistence, mobility and toxicity weight-of-evidence inputs.
A US aquatic tissue criterion cannot be treated as a water-column PNEC.
A reviewed external site model preserves inputs, version, hashes, mapped endpoints and reviewer decision.
A current source check is required when an instrument is marked proposed, interim, nonbinding or living guidance.
